title: How much more may agents do in a project you trust?
context: Matt wants personal projects to give agents more room than work repos. Today each repo is Ask or Auto (decision 34); in Auto, contained work runs on its own, and the hard stops (rules entry R005) are the same in every repo and fixed in code. This decision sets what a third level, Trusted, adds. Whatever is picked, some stops stay at every level (Claude's judgement): force push, rewriting pushed history, deleting branches, pushing straight to main (C005), writes outside the project or its worktrees and temp folders (including ~/.claude and ~/crux), secrets, stopping or restarting the live hub, system-wide installers, and any send, share or delete through mail, calendar or drive (R006). Trusted can be set only from the hub page, never from the repo's own .crux-hub.json, so a cloned repo cannot trust itself. Amends decision 34 and rules entry R005; option B would also change the core rule that merges are always Matt's (decision 22).

options.name: Installs and the open web, merges stay yours
options.summary: Trusted = Auto, plus installing packages into the project (npm, pip) and reading or downloading from any website into the project. Merging to main still comes to you.
pros: Removes the cards that slow personal work most (installs, looking things up)
Keeps the core rule: you merge after click-testing
cons: A package or a download can carry bad code into the project; you see it at review, not before

options.name: A, plus the orchestrator merges after a review
options.summary: As A, and in a Trusted project the orchestrator may merge a code pull request once a reviewer has passed it and the tests are green, reporting it in one line. You click-test on main afterwards.
pros: Personal projects move without waiting for your merge word
cons: Breaks the core rule that you merge after click-testing, for those projects
Visible changes reach main before you have seen them

options.name: No Trusted level for now
options.summary: Keep Ask and Auto; just move the settings onto the screen (decision 44).
cons: Personal projects keep the same install and web cards as work repos

recommendation: A removes the cards that slow personal projects without touching the merge rule you settled; B can follow later for a project where you want it.
reason: Matt: "install packages, open web, merge after a review with owner permission" (and to the mockup worker: "Yes, an orchestrator can do the merges, but needs permission."). So in a Trusted project the orchestrator runs the merge itself after a reviewer has passed it, but only once the owner says yes to that merge; the merge never happens on the orchestrator's own judgement.

settles.value: per repo: Ask, Auto, or Trusted (set only from the hub page); fixed stops at every level: force push, history rewrite, branch deletion, push to main, writes outside the project, secrets, the live hub, system-wide installs, outward connector actions
